title: routing-and-controlplane-runbook-architecture-notes
content:
Purpose
This doc is a combined architecture + operational runbook for our routing policy engine and control-plane components across multi-region deployments. It is intentionally practical: short diagnostics, commands, and mitigations embedded in architecture context so on-call engineers can both reason about root cause and act quickly.

Scope
- Components: routing-policy-service (RPS), control-plane-api, policy-store (etcd/consul), route-agent (edge sidecar), regional health aggregator, and the global policy router.
- Cross-region concerns: affinity, KV replication lag, split-brain on leader election, and fallback model variant routing.
- Not included: serving-runtime GPU node-level debugging (see serving-runtime/sre-runbooks).

Architecture notes (brief)
- Control plane (control-plane-api + policy-store) is the single source of truth for routing policies, rollout stages, and region weightings. It exposes a versioned API used by route-agents to fetch policies on startup and at policy-change webhooks.
- Route-agents run in each region and maintain an in-memory policy cache and local evaluation engine for low-latency routing decisions. Agents watch the policy-store via streaming endpoints and apply delta updates.
- Policy evaluation order: explicit-route (customer pin) -> canary -> weighted-routing -> geo-affinity -> fallback. Policies are deterministic and evaluated top-to-bottom.
- Rollouts: canaries are enabled by rollout rules stored in the policy-store. Each rollout has a name, window, and metric criteria (latency and error thresholds).
- Health checks: agents report region-level health via health-aggregator which updates a region-status index used by global router.

Common incident scenarios + runbooks
1) Control plane API unresponsive (HTTP 5xx or timeouts)
- Symptom: config change fails; route-agents show repeated fetch retries; recent deploy of control-plane-api; alerts: PLAT-CONTROL-API-ERR.
- Quick checks:
  - Check SLOs/dashboard: control_plane_api_request_latency_p50/p95, control_plane_api_error_rate (Dash: Platform / Control Plane / API)
  - kubectl -n platform get pods -l app=control-plane-api; kubectl logs -f deployment/control-plane-api -c api --tail 200
  - curl -v https://control-plane-api.internal/healthz || echo "down"
- Quick mitigations:
  - If pods are CrashLoopBackOff: kubectl describe pod <pod> to see OOM or config errors. Revert recent config change (kubectl rollout undo deployment/control-plane-api) if deploy timestamp aligns with incident.
  - If high CPU due to policy-store scan: scale up replicas temporarily: kubectl scale deploy/control-plane-api --replicas=4 (notify infra).
  - If external dependency (auth/KMS) failing: flip maintained feature-flag to allow unauthenticated local reads for emergency: POST to admin toggle endpoint (requires infra approval).
- Recovery steps:
  - Redeploy last known-good image: kubectl set image deployment/control-plane-api control-plane-api=registry.redwood/internal/control-plane-api:stable-20260201
  - Validate route-agents reconnected: check route-agent logs and policy version: kubectl logs -l app=route-agent -c agent | grep "policy_version="
- Post-incident:
  - Open PLAT JIRA ticket, attach timeline and last deploy id (PLAT-CONTROL-API-ERR-YYYYMMDD), run postmortem template, update changelog.

2) Policy drift or incorrect evaluation order deployed (bad rollout rules)
- Symptom: certain traffic unexpectedly hits a fallback model; regression alerts on quality (Rerank/quality evals) or sudden cost increase.
- Quick checks:
  - Check policy versions: curl https://control-plane-api.internal/v1/policies/versions last_3
  - Search for recent policy changes: git log --since="48 hours" -- platform-configs/policies
  - Query route-agent logs for "policy-eval" traces and decision path: kubectl logs -l app=route-agent | egrep "policy_eval|decision_path"
- Quick mitigations:
  - Push emergency policy patch that restores previous rule ordering. Use the policy-store admin UI to revert version or use API: POST /v1/policies/revert {"version":"v123"}
  - If automatic rollouts continue to apply bad policy, disable rollout engine: PATCH /v1/admin/settings {"rollout_enabled":false} (only for <30m).
- Recovery steps:
  - Validate behavior in canary region and run synthetic tests (see linked_artifacts). Promote fix to all regions after 30 minutes of stable metrics.

3) Regional split-brain / KV replication lag causing inconsistent policies across regions
- Symptom: region A has new policies, region B still uses older policies -> inconsistent routing; alerts: PLAT-POLICY-REPL-LAG.
- Quick checks:
  - Check policy-store replication status: kubectl -n platform exec -it statefulset/policy-store -- /bin/psql -c "SELECT * FROM replication_status;"
  - Check agent-sync metrics: route_agent_policy_sync_lag_seconds{region="us-east-1"}
  - Look for leader-election warnings in logs: kubectl logs -l app=policy-store | egrep "leader|raft|election"
- Quick mitigations:
  - If leader elected incorrectly, force leader stepdown to trigger re-election: kubectl exec -it pod/policy-store-0 -- /bin/consul operator raft remove-peer <peer-id> (follow infra runbook) or use etcdctl to promote leader.
  - Temporarily set global routing to prefer region with majority policy consistency: POST /v1/admin/routing/override {"global_prefer":"us-west-2"}
- Recovery steps:
  - Reconcile KV store: run the replication repair script from git (scripts/repair-kv-replication.sh) with oncall approval. Monitor sync lag and then lift routing override.

4) Route-agent high-latency evaluation causing end-to-end latency spikes
- Symptom: route-agent CPU usage high, p99 eval latency elevated, affecting latency SLOs.
- Quick checks:
  - route_agent_eval_latency_p50/p95/p99, route_agent_cpu_usage
  - Check rule set size: POST /v1/admin/policies/size for region to see number of rules loaded
- Quick mitigations:
  - Reduce policy complexity: enable emergency-compact policy set: POST /v1/admin/policies/compact {"reason":"latency_immediate"} to temporarily apply simplified ruleset.
  - Scale route-agent horizontally: kubectl scale deployment/route-agent --replicas=<current*2>
- Recovery steps:
  - Run policy pruning process to remove obsolete legacy rules (ticket PLAT-3120). Re-introduce full rule set gradually via canary.

Investigations / diagnostics cheat-sheet
- Verify control-plane health: curl https://control-plane-api.internal/metrics | egrep "control_plane_api|policy_store"
- Agent status per region: curl https://health-aggregator.internal/regions | jq . (look for last_synced_ts)
- Policy version reported to router: curl https://global-router.internal/status | jq '.policy_version'
- Example kubectl debugging commands:
  - kubectl -n platform exec -it deploy/control-plane-api -- curl -sS localhost:8080/debug/vars | jq .
  - kubectl logs -l app=route-agent -c agent --since=30m | egrep "warn|error|policy_eval"

Escalation and ownership
- First responder: oncall-platform (rotation). If control-plane API >15m, escalate to platform-sre lead and platform eng owner.
- Pager escalation policy: see PLAT-SOP-ESCL (Confluence link in linked_artifacts). Provide timeline, last_playbook_steps, and any admin toggles we exercised.

Safety knobs and feature flags (where to flip things)
- rollout_enabled (boolean) - disables automated rollouts when false. Admin API path: /v1/admin/settings
- policy_store_read_fallback - allows route-agents to use cached policies for longer TTL when set.
- global_routing_override - temporarily forces traffic to a single region or traffic tier. Use only for short windows and record justification.

Templates / quick commands
- Revert control-plane deployment: kubectl rollout undo deployment/control-plane-api -n platform
- Scale route-agent: kubectl scale deploy/route-agent -n platform --replicas=6
- Force policy-store leader election: kubectl exec statefulset/policy-store-0 -n platform -- /usr/local/bin/raftctl transfer-leader --target-id=<id>
- Emergency compact policy (API): curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://control-plane-api.internal/v1/admin/policies/compact -d '{"reason":"latency_immediate"}'

Post-incident checklist
- Create JIRA ticket with affected regions, start/end times, deploy ids, and mitigations taken (labels: incident, control-plane).
- Add timeline to ticket and link to this doc.
- Run policy audit: ensure no manual emergency edits remain. Archive emergency policy versions to policy-store/history.
- Update runbook with any new commands, gotchas, or learned metrics.

Known gaps / follow-ups
- No safe automated rollback from policy migrations that touch more than 500 rules. Action: implement transactional policy-apply with preflight dry-run (PLAT-4010).
- No RBAC approval flow for emergency admin toggles. Action: short-term Slack approval step required; long-term: implement approval queue.

Appendix: useful dashboards and tests
- Dashboards: Platform / Control Plane / Policy Store Replication; Platform / Routing / Agent Latency; Platform / Global Router Health.
- Synthetic tests: per-region policy-eval synthetic (synthetic/policy-eval) that runs every 30s; endpoint: https://synthetic.internal/policy-eval?test=basic-route

Contact list (oncall rotation owners)
- platform-oncall: @platform-oncall (pager), lead: Arjun Patel <arjun@redwood.com>, eng-owner: Maya Chen <maya.chen@redwood.com>

Notes to self (working area)
- Need to add TLS cert rotation steps for policy-store replication (deferred to infra).
- Double-check rollback image tags used in last 3 control-plane deploys.
- Follow up: add example logs for policy-eval decision_path so new oncall can grep them quicker.

End of doc.
